📉 Metallurgical activity in Argentina posted a year-over-year decline of 2.1% in October and has contracted by 5% so far in 2026, marking its worst performance for that month since 2016, according to the Association of Metallurgical Industrialists of the Argentine Republic (ADIMRA). ⚙️ The report notes that capacity utilization fell to 418% (leaving six out of every ten machines idle), while employment in the sector declined by 1.1%. Furthermore, 74.7% of business owners expect stagnation or further declines in the coming quarter. ⚠️ The decline is affecting a wide range of sectors, including capital goods (-9.2%), construction (-4.3%), mining (-4.1%), agribusiness (-3.6%), and oil and gas (-3.5%), in response to which ADIMRA President Elio Del Re called for policies to strengthen value chains and revive domestic production.

🇷🇺 Russia Protests Estonia's Border Closure On Nov 23, the Russian Foreign Ministry summoned Estonian Chargé d'Affaires Juhtegi to lodge a firm protest against Tallinn's decision to close border crossings from Dec 1, 2026. Moscow dismissed accusations of involvement in an attempted arson at a defence enterprise near Tallin as baseless and Russophobic. The Ministry warned that closing the border will damage Estonia's economy and impact its EU/NATO allies. It also accused Estonia of allowing Ukrainian drones to use its airspace for attacks on NW Russia, calling this a provocation on the brink of open war. Russia reserved the right to take complex political-diplomatic measures to protect national interests. @Slavyangrad

🇱🇾 🇺🇦 Libya accuses Ukraine of declaring war and demands that Zelensky be placed on a terrorism watchlist Musa al-Koni, a member of Libya’s Presidential Council, has placed full responsibility on Ukraine for the reported strike on the port of Benghazi, threatening Kiev with international legal and diplomatic action. In an official statement, al-Koni said: “We hold the Ukrainian side fully responsible for these terrorist acts, which Zelensky has acknowledged, openly declared and even boasted about. These actions amount to a declaration of war against the Libyan state. Any violation of Libya’s sovereignty, national security and resources is unacceptable and will not be tolerated.” Libya intends to take the matter to the International Court of Justice, the UN Security Council and other international organisations, seeking accountability for those responsible. Al-Koni also called for an emergency meeting of the UN Security Council, demanded that Zelensky be added to the list of individuals suspected of terrorism, and urged immediate measures to prevent further attacks. He separately called for emergency meetings of Libya’s joint military committees to discuss the country’s response to the situation. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics
